You guys are responsible for the Vietnam War and military deaths around the world. Why would I take a computer from you knowing that it’s from the military? You’re going to use this computer to spy on me, man. You’re going to turn me into a robot. I’m not touching this computer. But it’s coming from Steve Jobs. That’s different, right? Oh, Steve Jobs. He’s a visionary and messianic. Of course, I’ll buy this personal computer from him.

At this time in history, America is at war with the Soviet Union. Which system is better: communism or capitalism? If you said that the government spent billions of dollars to build technology proving communism was better, but if it’s these guys working alone in Silicon Valley who came up with ideas proving capitalism and entrepreneurship were better, then the US government built this knowledge, so it belongs to the American people. How do you monetize public knowledge when creating private companies controlled by secret societies?

That makes perfect sense, right? Bill Gates, [snorts], Al Gore—they’re just front people. They’re not at the wheel; it’s the real control of society. Another example is Google. The American military spent billions of dollars to build the fiber optic network that forms the base of the internet. These two guys in their 20s took over this network and created Google. It’s like when the government spends billions building a highway, and you come along to put up toll booths. Why were they allowed to do that? And now they’re slowly building their own underwater fiber optic network, basically privatizing what was built by the American military. Yes, they’re spending their own money, but it’s taxpayers who funded the R&D for all this. Mark Zuckerberg isn’t that smart; he stole his idea from Harvard classmates and got billions of dollars from venture capitalists to start Facebook. But Yahoo offered him a billion dollars to buy Facebook—they’d give him a lot of money. Why didn’t he take it? Because he’s 19, has no experience, never failed in his life, and is likely suffering from hubris.

Amazon, Google, and Apple are successful because they have Steve Jobs, control the world search, and control buying things, respectively. But what does Facebook do that’s so great? There’s an explanation: this success is part of a bigger picture.
